title: Submit button disabled when mandatory fields are empty
gherkin:
Feature: Registration Form Submit Button Behavior
  Scenario: Submit button remains disabled when all mandatory fields are empty
    Given the registration form is displayed
    When no fields are filled
    Then the Submit button should be disabled
rationale: Validates core requirement that submit button remains disabled until all mandatory fields are filled. This is the foundational behavior for mandatory field enforcement.
usedContextItems: Submit button remains disabled until all mandatory fields are filled and the legal consent checkbox is checked
generationSummary: Generated 10 executable Gherkin tests for R1 (Registration mandatory fields). Tests cover mandatory field validation, submit button behavior, Terms and Conditions consent requirements, email uniqueness (case-insensitive), and OWASP compliance for email enumeration prevention. All tests are grounded in the operative context and supporting evidence, excluding conflicting proposals from JIRA-Auth-114 and JIRA-Auth-111.
resolvedOperativeContext: Submit button remains disabled until all mandatory fields are filled and the legal consent checkbox is checked || Registration form must include a Terms and Conditions checkbox representing acceptance of both Terms of Service and Privacy Policy || All fields are mandatory and must be validated before submission.
resolvedExceptions: Email uniqueness validation must be case-insensitive (e.g., Test@t.com equals test@t.com) || 'If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it' (prevents email enumeration per OWASP compliance)
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: JIRA-Auth-114 proposes making phone number optional, contradicting the primary requirement that phone number is mandatory || JIRA-Auth-111 proposes allowing multiple users to share the same email address if phone number is unique, contradicting the email uniqueness requirement
resolutionNotes: >E1 provides the core specification with mandatory fields and form behavior. E4 clarifies field structure (separate first/last name, optional middle name). E3 and E7 provide validation details for phone and email. E6 introduces a critical compliance conflict regarding consent capture methodology. E8 and E9 present conflicting proposals about phone number and email uniqueness that contradict the primary requirement. E10 provides supporting context from the configuration specification. E11 reinforces the disabled-submit behavior. E12 documents the email uniqueness contradiction explicitly. title: OWASP compliance: Email enumeration prevention message
gherkin:
Feature: OWASP Email Enumeration Prevention
  Scenario: Generic message displayed regardless of email existence
    Given the registration form is displayed
    When a user submits the form with email "existing@example.com"
    And the email already exists in the system
    Then the message "If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it" should be displayed
    When a user submits the form with email "nonexistent@example.com"
    And the email does not exist in the system
    Then the same message "If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it" should be displayed
rationale: Validates OWASP compliance exception that prevents email enumeration attacks by displaying an identical message regardless of whether the email exists in the system.
